questions.q: How does the Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit or a CIS Benchmark actually get applied to an environment in practice?
options: By running a single PowerShell cmdlet that applies the entire internet's worth of settings automatically
Baselines cannot be applied through Group Policy at all
By manually re-typing every individual setting into a new GPO from the published PDF
By importing the baseline's GPO backup into a new GPO via GPMC's Import Settings wizard
questions.explain: Both SCT and CIS Benchmark baselines ship as GPO backups; GPMC's Import Settings wizard loads that backup's settings into a new GPO in minutes.

questions.q: A baseline disables SMBv1 everywhere, but one legacy printer requires it. What is the correct way to handle that exception?
options: Edit the SMBv1 setting directly inside the baseline GPO so it applies to every machine
Create a second, narrowly-scoped GPO (e.g. with a WMI filter) that re-enables SMBv1 only for that machine, leaving the baseline GPO untouched
Disable the entire baseline GPO until the printer is replaced
Ignore the printer and let it stop working
questions.explain: Editing the baseline itself would quietly remove that protection fleet-wide. A separate, narrowly-scoped exception GPO keeps the baseline intact everywhere else.

questions.q: What is a pilot OU used for when rolling out a new baseline GPO?
options: A naming convention with no functional effect on Group Policy
Permanently excluding certain departments from ever receiving the baseline
Storing a backup copy of the GPO in case it needs to be restored later
Linking the new GPO to a small, representative slice of machines first, to catch problems before an org-wide rollout
questions.explain: A pilot OU lets the team watch for breakage on a representative subset of machines before the baseline reaches the entire organization.

questions.q: During a pilot period, what should the team actually be monitoring?
options: Nothing — a pilot period is purely a waiting period with no monitoring involved
Stock price of the vendor who published the baseline
Only whether the GPO successfully imported, with no further checks needed
gpresult output on pilot machines, Event Viewer for new audit/lockout events, and the help desk queue
questions.explain: The pilot period is only useful if someone actively checks policy application and real-world impact on pilot machines during that window.

questions.q: Why is importing a baseline GPO backup preferable to configuring the equivalent settings by hand, one at a time?
options: GPMC does not support manually configuring individual settings at all
Hand-configuring settings is actually faster in every case
It applies hundreds of tested settings in minutes with no manual re-typing and no risk of a typo in a setting's path or value
Imported settings cannot later be customized or overridden
questions.explain: The whole point of importing a tested GPO backup is speed and accuracy — avoiding the inconsistency that hand-configuring hundreds of settings invites.
